title: DC-area forecast: Humidity increases late tonight. Heat returns Sunday.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Late afternoon and evening temperatures near 80 slowly sag to lows that range through the 60s. Just a few clouds and patches of fog possible near dawn.

What's next? Heat and humidity arrive Sunday and set up camp for the week. Heat indexes during the coming week feel more like July with midweek feeling near 105 in the hottest, steamiest spots. Afternoon shower and storm chances return Sunday and slowly increase during the heat wave.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Still fairly comfortable with lows in the 60s, but humidity increases, with dew points near 70 possible by dawn. Skies remain mostly clear until near dawn when a few clouds and patches of fog may develop. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow (Sunday): Heat and humidity are back. Highs in the mid-80s to around 90 feel as hot as the mid-90s thanks to dew points near 70. Winds from the south stay light at around 10 mph. Skies are partly sunny. A spotty shower or weak storm is possible during the mid- to late afternoon. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: After any brief evening shower or storm, it's just really muggy. Lows only dip near 70 to mid-70s. Skies are partly cloudy and winds from the south are light. Confidence: Medium-High

📬 Get our forecast in your inbox

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

The heat is on. Highs reach the low to mid-90s Monday and mid-90s Tuesday and Wednesday under partly sunny skies. High humidity Tuesday and Wednesday (dew points near 70) helps heat indexes rise into the upper 90s to near 100, adding to the hot and muggy feel. Each day has a chance of an isolated late-day shower or storm. Confidence: Medium

Highs could still be well into the 90s Thursday, with perhaps a higher chance of scattered showers and storms as a cold front moves into the region. That front should help temperatures trend back down to highs in the 80s, if not by Friday then at least for the Labor Day weekend.

Today’s daily digit — 7/10: A solid late-summer day, with lower humidity, plenty of sunshine and no rain to worry about. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for August 29

Unseasonable chill in 1986 tied a record low for August, while in 1988 the remnants of Tropical Storm Chris brought soaking rains and gusty winds to the region.
